hints: Focus on shifting the equilibrium to the right, since more product means a greater percentage of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$.
Notice that $\Delta H = -57 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, so the forward reaction is exothermic and is favoured by low temperature.
Count the gas moles, 2 on the left but only 1 on the right, then link that to how pressure shifts the position to give the winning combination.
walkthrough:
**State the goal clearly**

We want the greatest percentage of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$. That means we want the equilibrium position shifted as far right as possible.

$$2\text{NO}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons \text{N}_2\text{O}_4(g)$$

**Use temperature to favour the exothermic direction**

The forward reaction has $\Delta H = -57 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, so it releases heat. By Le Chatelier's principle, lowering the temperature favours the exothermic direction to produce more heat.

So low temperature shifts equilibrium right toward $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$.

**Use pressure to favour fewer gas moles**

On the left there are 2 moles of gas, on the right only 1 mole of gas. Increasing pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules to reduce the pressure.

So high pressure shifts equilibrium right toward $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$.

**Combine both conditions**

Low temperature favours $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ and high pressure favours $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$. Together, high pressure with low temperature gives the maximum yield at equilibrium.

options.A: High pressure is correct because it favours 1 mole of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ over 2 moles of $\text{NO}_2$, but high temperature is wrong. High temperature favours the endothermic backward reaction, so it decomposes $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ back to $\text{NO}_2$.
options.B: High pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles, which is $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$. Low temperature favours the exothermic forward reaction, which also makes $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$. Both effects work together to give the greatest percentage of product.
options.C: This is the opposite of what is needed. Low pressure favours the side with more gas moles ($\text{NO}_2$) and high temperature favours the endothermic reverse reaction ($\text{NO}_2$ formation). This gives the least $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$.
options.D: Low temperature is correct because it favours the exothermic forward reaction, but low pressure is wrong. Low pressure shifts equilibrium left toward 2 moles of $\text{NO}_2$, reducing the percentage of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$.
